title: Run-IQ rule definition
description: A rule definition as accepted by normalizeRuleDefinition from @run-iq/spec. At the top level, null means absent for every optional field and every extension field. Top-level keys other than the named fields are plugin extensions: any JSON value. A rule of the reserved model @run-iq/exception has a non-empty exceptions list and no output (the default output value, or <own rule set>:value, means absent). The bounds effectiveFrom and effectiveUntil are both civil dates (YYYY-MM-DD) or both instants (D-13). Some rules are NOT expressible in JSON Schema and are checked only by validateRuleDefinition and normalizeRuleDefinition: effectiveUntil, when set, must be strictly after effectiveFrom (the half-open window [effectiveFrom, effectiveUntil) must not be empty); an instant must stay within the years 0000 to 9999 once its offset is applied; no text (effectiveOn included) may hold a lone UTF-16 surrogate; in a dimension spec, an except value must not repeat an anyOf value; a forEach.key list holds one name per level (one more than the '*' segments of forEach.path); each forEach.orderBy path appears once; forEach.segments.from and forEach.segments.until differ; a selector's ids name rules of the rule sets it targets (its ruleSets, else the rule's own rule set): an id of a rule set the selector does not target is refused; a selector's outputs name outputs of the rule's own rule set or of a rule set it targets: any other is refused; on a rule of the reserved model @run-iq/exception, an output value qualified by another rule set than the rule's own is refused (only the default output, value or <own rule set>:value, means absent).

id.description: A rule id: non-empty, without ':' (which separates a rule set from a name, D-4).

params.description: Required; any JSON value, null included (null is data here).

effectiveFrom.description: Inclusive start: a civil date, or an instant.

effectiveUntil.description: Exclusive end, of the same form as effectiveFrom; null or absent for no end. Must be after effectiveFrom (checked by validateRuleDefinition only).

timeZone.description: The time zone of the window: UTC, a fixed offset +HH:MM/-HH:MM (hour at most 23), or an IANA name Area/Location. +00:00 and -00:00 are normalized to UTC.

effectiveOn.description: The reference date of the window, a JSON pointer: /$dates/<name>, /$item/<path> (needs forEach) or /$segment/from (needs forEach.segments). No '-' segment.

forEach.description: What the rule iterates over: a collection { path, key, orderBy?, dimensions?, recurse?, groupBy? } or time segments { segments }. null means absent.

ruleSet.description: The rule set (pack) of the rule; null, absent and 'local' are a local rule.

dimensions.description: One dimension spec per dimension; a null value means the dimension is unset. Dimension names starting with $ are reserved (even unset).

exceptions.description: The exceptions the rule carries, in order. null and [] mean absent.

checksum.description: Ignored: never part of the definition.

allOf.description: The reserved model @run-iq/exception only carries exceptions: at least one, and no output. The default output (value, or <own rule set>:value) means absent.
Both bounds have the same form: a civil effectiveFrom goes with a civil effectiveUntil (D-13).
Both bounds have the same form: an instant effectiveFrom goes with an instant effectiveUntil (D-13).
effectiveOn on /$item/ needs a forEach with path and without groupBy: a segment and a group have no single item.

outputName.description: An output name (D-4): name or <rule set>:<name>, with at most one ':'. No '.' anywhere (a JSONLogic var would read it as a path); neither part starts with $ (reserved); the rule set part is a rule set id other than local (a local name is written bare); the name part is non-empty.

ruleDate.description: A civil date or an instant.

civilDate.description: A civil date YYYY-MM-DD that exists (proleptic Gregorian, years 0000 to 9999). It stays civil after normalization.

instant.description: An instant YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS with 0 to 3 decimals and Z or an offset +HH:MM/-HH:MM (uppercase T and Z, second 00 to 59, offset hour at most 23). A date-time without a time zone is refused. Normalized to YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ.

timeZone.description: UTC, +HH:MM/-HH:MM (hour at most 23, minute at most 59), or an IANA name: segments [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_+-]* separated by /, at least two, the first starting with an uppercase letter.

effectiveOn.description: A JSON pointer (RFC 6901) to a reference date: /$dates/<name> (one non-empty name), /$item/<path> or /$segment/from. A '-' segment is refused.

ruleException.description: One exception: inhibit the targeted rules, substitute params into them (deep merge), or short-circuit one output to a value.

params.description: Parameters deep-merged into the targeted rules' params.

ruleSelector.description: Fields combine by AND, the values of one field by OR; dimensions require every key to be written the same (normal form), never a membership. An empty field puts no constraint; at least one field must be non-empty. ruleSets lists the rule sets targeted (local for the rules without a rule set); absent, only the rule set of the rule that carries the exception. ruleSets alone does not constrain a selector. Bare ids and outputs designate the carrier's rule set, qualified ones the named rule set.

dimensionValue.description: A dimension value: a non-empty code, or <system>:<code> (the first ':' separates; both parts non-empty).

dimensionSpec.description: What a rule asks of one dimension: a value (equality), or { ref?, anyOf, except?, match? }. except needs ref. With ref, the values of anyOf and except are unqualified (no ':'): the referential fixes the code system. NOT expressible in JSON Schema, checked only by validateRuleDefinition and normalizeRuleDefinition: an except value must not repeat an anyOf value.

ruleRef.description: A rule cited by a selector: id or <rule set>:<id>, with at most one ':'; the rule set part is a rule set id other than local (a local id is written bare).

ruleSetId.description: A rule set id (D-4): lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-'; no '.' (a version is never part of the id, and every qualified name stays readable by every DSL). local names the rules without a rule set.

forEach.description: A collection or time segments. Literal segments of a path never start with @ or ! (they mark subjects, D-2); pointers into an element name one value (no '*' segment) and hold no '-' segment. NOT expressible in JSON Schema, checked only by validateRuleDefinition and normalizeRuleDefinition: a key list holds one name per level; each orderBy path appears once; segments.from and segments.until differ.

path.description: A JSON pointer into the input data; each '*' segment steps into the elements of a list (one level per list). It starts and ends with a member name, never has two '*' in a row, and does not start with $ (an engine variable).

key.description: The member that identifies the elements: one name for every level, or a list of one name per level.

orderBy.description: The rank of the elements: keys compared in order; elements equal on every key are tied (AMBIGUOUS_ORDER for an instance that reads its rank). [] means absent.

dimensions.description: Dimensions read per element: a name (not starting with $) to a pointer into the element. {} means absent.

recurse.description: A pointer into the element to its child list; no segment starting with @ or !.

allOf.description: recurse and groupBy cannot be combined.
A group has no single element: groupBy excludes dimensions.
groupBy excludes orderBy for now: the order of groups is not defined yet.

facts.description: Facts whose changes cut the period: pointers into the input data, not to an engine variable ($), naming one value.

elementPointer.description: A JSON pointer into the element: not empty, no '*' (it names one value) and no '-' segment.

namedDate.description: A named date of the input: /$dates/<name>.
